checks.question: Is the expanded two-step B_1 endpoint proof correct?
evidence: Proposition 1, manuscript/paper.tex:342-363, defines B_R over probability vectors with L1 radius 2R; lines 355-357 explicitly state: any two simplex points have L1 distance at most 2, B_1 is the full simplex, and the linear objective is maximized at a vertex, hence V(1)=max_K g(K).

The first implication is correct because for simplex points q and H-hat, ||q-H-hat||_1 <= ||q||_1+||H-hat||_1 = 2. Thus every simplex q lies in B_1, while the definition already constrains B_1 to the simplex.
The second implication is correct because a linear functional over a finite simplex attains its maximum at a vertex e_K, with value g(K).
The same proposition correctly retains the general curve as a capacity-constrained, nondecreasing, piecewise-linear LP and explicitly rejects global affinity.
